prompt.en: Two stations decide to leave a repeater for simplex. One operator says the new frequency quickly and changes channels before the other station acknowledges it. What is the procedural error?

text.en: They should confirm that both stations copied the destination before either station leaves the repeater.
They should keep talking on the repeater because direct-path contacts are never a courteous option.
They should double transmitter power before changing channels so the move sounds official.
They should send a tuner carrier on the repeater output before announcing the move.

explanation.en: A channel move fails if one station disappears before the other has copied the destination. Confirm the move first, then change channels.

prompt.en: Which action would NOT help keep a busy repeater available for other stations?

text.en: Leave a short gap after each over so another station can identify.
Use concise overs instead of filling the timer with one long transmission.
Move an extended direct-path chat to a suitable simplex channel.
Hold the microphone until the timer stops you because the controller will protect everyone else.

explanation.en: The timer is a safety backstop, not an operating method. Courtesy means leaving gaps, keeping overs short, and moving suitable conversations away from the repeater.

prompt.en: A handheld is strong into a local repeater site but the programmed access tone is wrong. What result should the operator expect?

text.en: The repeater may receive RF energy but not repeat usable audio for everyone else.
The repeater will automatically translate the wrong tone into the coordinated tone.
The two-metre offset will change from 600 kHz to 800 kHz.
Other stations will hear a louder signal because tones add transmitter power.

explanation.en: A correct CTCSS setting is an access condition. Signal strength alone does not guarantee that the repeater opens and retransmits the audio.
